messages:
maria (Support): Heads-up — we got a customer escalation from BrightFleet: p95 and p99 latency jumped for their account starting ~08:10 UTC. They say API timeouts and billing retries.
oncall-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike on /v1/generate for tenant brightfleet (region: us-east-1). Started 2026-03-15T08:10:12Z. Current p99: 2.8s, baseline 0.35s. Incident ID INC-24123.
lee (Eng-Oncall): looking. Is this global or account-scoped? Any auth errors in the logs?
maria (Support): BrightFleet sent logs: many 504s and a few auth 401s mixed in. They reported increased retry loops from the client causing billing issues.
james (SRE): I pulled metrics — the host-level tail shows a short-lived queueing event on the pool that serves dedicated-capacity for BrightFleet. p95 jumped from 300ms -> 1.1s for a 6m window, p99 to 2.8s. Attaching the prom query I used: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,instance,tenant))`.
olivia (Telemetry): quick note: our dashboard panel uses rollup-derived p99 (preaggregated per-minute summaries) while support's alert is using raw histogram query. They can diverge if buckets got re-binned or if we switched exporter recently.
lee (Eng-Oncall): ah — did we recently change histogram bucket boundaries for the C++ runtime? I remember a PR adjusting bins for quantized kernels.
james (SRE): yes, there was a runtime telemetry tweak yesterday to add finer buckets above 500ms to diagnose tail for attention kernels. That will change histogram rollups for older samples.
maria (Support): Customer insists dashboard showed normal numbers then suddenly alerts fired — they screenshotted the Console p99 as ~0.4s at 08:09 and then 2.6s at 08:11. They want explanation to billing team.
olivia (Telemetry): likely cause: rollup path used by Console queries relies on aggregated minute-level counters which were backfilled differently after the bucket change. The live raw histogram query (used by alert) picks up immediate bucket counts and shows the spike.
lee (Eng-Oncall): can we reproduce? Steps I ran: 1) switch tenant header X-Tenant: brightfleet; 2) run `ab -n 100 -c 10` against /v1/generate with a small prompt; 3) monitor `istio_request_duration_seconds_bucket` for that tenant. I saw the p99 jump only on raw histogram queries when the test overlapped with a rolling deploy.
maria (Support): BrightFleet also saw increased client retries which inflated server queue — they sent a snippet: `Status: 504, attempt 3 of 5, retry-after: 1s`.
james (SRE): mitigation: 1) temporary rate-limit per-tenant at the edge to smooth retries, 2) pin BrightFleet traffic to a new dedicated pool (if available), 3) revert the bucket-change PR for rollup compatibility if confirmed causing confusion.
lee (Eng-Oncall): immediate action — enable tenant-level throttling to cap concurrent requests to 60 for brightfleet; that should break the retry amplification. I'll patch config now.
olivia (Telemetry): I'm adding a note to the Console panel: "This panel shows rollup-derived percentiles; for debug use raw histograms (Debug > Raw p99)." Also adding a quick query that shows both sources side-by-side for 30m.
maria (Support): I'll reply to BrightFleet: explain suspected telemetry divergence and that we're applying tenant throttling while we investigate permanent fixes. Also offer to credit billing for retries during the spike window.
oncall-bot: ACTION: tenant throttling rule applied for brightfleet by lee at 2026-03-15T08:20:03Z. Monitor for recovery.
james (SRE): follow-up: after throttle, p95 returned to ~350ms in 4 minutes and p99 to ~420ms. Looks like retry amplification was the amplifier; bucket-change caused dashboard confusion. We should schedule a postmortem and decide on rollup compatibility policy.
maria (Support): noted. I'll keep customer updated and draft a short postmortem email. :thumbsup:
lee (Eng-Oncall): good. I'll open a runbook PR for tenant throttling steps and a rollback playbook for the histogram bucket change. tagging olivia and james. @olivia @james please add telemetry notes to the PM.
olivia (Telemetry): will do. I'll also add an automated check: when we change histogram buckets, create a transient overlay that keeps previous rollup buckets for 1 hour to avoid UI jumps.
maria (Support): closing loop with customer: "we applied throttling and saw metrics recover; we will credit retries and follow up with a postmortem within 48 hours."
